category_path_en: Discrimination Based on Other Physical/Psychological Differences (Physical, Psychological, Pregnancy Status, Genetic Information)
title: Personal attacks/social exclusion and incitement to violence targeting specific feature groups
source_text: Personal attacks/social exclusion and incitement to violence targeting specific feature groups: Advocating or glorifying verbal insults/body shaming against those with specific appearance features/pregnant women/carriers of specific genes, inciting exclusion/isolation/mockery against those with specific physiological function abnormalities/minor psychological issues/pregnant women, promoting or rationalizing "pregnancy violence"/"fetal discrimination" against pregnant women, providing or implying organizing illegal rallies/protests or attack actions targeting specific physical/psychological feature groups/pregnant women/genetic information groups, publishing content with threatening/inciting language intended to intimidate or belittle those with specific physical/psychological features/pregnant women/carriers of specific genes.

elements.label: Bias based on physical appearance
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies targeting individuals due to their physical appearance, including body shaming or verbal insults.
bias_surfaces: derogatory generalizations about aesthetic traits
normative framing of bodily features as deviant
exclusionary social narratives tied to looks
dehumanizing rhetoric based on visible characteristics
mockery framed as humor about appearance
hierarchical valuation of physical traits

elements.label: Bias based on genetic information
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies targeting individuals based on their genetic makeup or carrier status, including promotion of genetic profiling.
bias_surfaces: essentialist claims linking genes to worth or behavior
advocacy for genetic screening as gatekeeping
stigmatization of hereditary traits or conditions
deterministic narratives about genetic destiny
exclusion based on probabilistic health risks
moral judgment tied to inherited characteristics

elements.label: Bias based on physiological function
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies targeting individuals with atypical or impaired physiological functions, including mockery or exclusion.
bias_surfaces: pathologizing natural functional variation
social devaluation of non-normative bodily processes
ridicule of adaptive behaviors or assistive needs
framing functional differences as deficits
exclusion from normative social expectations
othering through medicalized language

elements.label: Bias based on pregnancy status
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies targeting individuals because they are pregnant, including incitement to violence or social exclusion.
bias_surfaces: stigmatization of reproductive capacity
framing pregnancy as a liability or burden
incitement against pregnant individuals in public discourse
normalization of pregnancy-related hostility
exclusion from social or institutional participation
rationalization of discriminatory practices during pregnancy

elements.label: Bias based on psychological condition
elements.risk_pattern: Unfair or biased tendencies targeting individuals with minor or atypical psychological conditions, including stigmatization or incitement to isolate.
bias_surfaces: conflation of mental health variance with danger
trivialization or mockery of emotional experiences
social ostracism based on perceived instability
moral blame for neurocognitive differences
denial of agency based on diagnostic labels
fear-based narratives about psychological diversity

quality_warnings: Stage 2 incorrectly added standalone mechanism elements (e.g., social_exclusion_mechanism) despite explicit_axes being non-empty; per Stage 1 rules, mechanisms must appear only within bias_surfaces of axis-aligned elements.
Mechanism concepts like 'incitement to violence' and 'stigmatization' should be reflected in the bias_surfaces of each axis-specific element rather than as separate elements.
All explicit axes from Stage 1 are preserved correctly, but redundant abstract mechanism elements violate normalization policy.
